clue.text: Dock worker, one having lost a few pounds?

definitions.meaning: a bargeman who ferries goods between ships and quays in a harbour

definitions.text: one having lost a few pounds?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a fellow who now weighs less after slimming

explanation.surface: A docker who has been dieting.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargeman working cargo in a port is the trade name; the second reading splits it into a slimmer fellow.

clue.text: Fitting one after another

definitions.meaning: proper or permissible, as a point raised at a meeting may be

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both appropriate under the rules of procedure and arranged in sequence.

clue.text: Huge crowd in store, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is spoken and its sound-alike written

parts.note: a store is a hoard, a stockpile

explanation.surface: A vast throng packed into a shop, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large unruly mass of people, a synonym for a huge crowd.

clue.text: Mysterious coteries formed

indicators.note: formed says the letters of the word before it are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: Exclusive little cliques have been set up, shrouded in mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' rearranges COTERIES; the surface sense of the cliques is apt, since secret knowledge belongs to an inner circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by an initiated few, hence obscure or mysterious.

clue.text: Fat appearing in eg a dad's prime — led astray?

indicators.note: astray says the letters before it have wandered out of their order

parts.note: taken with its S as a letter

explanation.surface: A father in his prime is putting on weight around the waist, led into bad habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges EG A DADS PRIME LED, all fifteen letters, into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the paunch people put on in their forties and fifties, a kind of fat.

clue.text: Sister outside a church in shade

indicators.note: outside says the nun's letters go round the next piece

parts.note: a Sister is a nun, a member of a religious order
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun stands outside a church in the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade of meaning is a subtle variation, the sense of this word.

clue.text: Exaggerated the military life

definitions.meaning: theatrically over the top, affected in manner
army life, as in the military ... or establishment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both affectedly theatrical and a place where soldiers are quartered, standing for army life.

clue.text: Famous English golfer's directed towards twigs

parts.note: Henry Cotton won the Open three times; with the 's his name gives the letters plus S
on, as in aimed on or at a target

explanation.surface: A celebrated golfer is pointed at the twigs of the rough.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cotton was a great English golfer of the 1930s and 40s. 'Twigs' is a verb here: understands.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal for to understand, and cotton on is a colloquial phrasal verb with the same meaning.

clue.text: Curse male accompanied by girl

parts.note: Alison is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Cursing the man who turned up with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Malison is an archaic word for a curse, the opposite of a benison.

clue.text: Excursion to ancient Sumerian city

parts.note: Ur was a city of ancient Sumer in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A trip to see the ruins of a city in Mesopotamia.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey or outing visiting places, a synonym for excursion.

clue.text: Tailor is called to Spanish region

indicators.note: to tailor is to cut and fit to shape, so these letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A tailor is summoned to an area of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' looks like a person being called; it is the verb that rearranges IS CALLED TO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the historic northern part of Castile in central Spain, a region.

clue.text: Stick plug in this place

parts.note: a plug is a piece of advertising, an ad
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Put an advert up in this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to something, a synonym for stick as a verb.

clue.text: A centre in the French ball game

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
in football to centre the ball is to cross it into the middle

explanation.surface: A player puts the ball in from the wing in a French match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' is the football verb, sending the ball into the middle, which is also called a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with a ball and netted sticks, so a ball game.

clue.text: Unfaithful daughter of priest is scared, shaken

indicators.note: shaken says the letters before it are jolted out of order

explanation.surface: A faithless priest's daughter is frightened and trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken' rearranges IS SCARED. In the Troy legend she is the daughter of the seer Calchas who abandons Troilus for Diomedes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chaucer and Shakespeare she is the Trojan priest Calchas's daughter who betrays her lover Troilus.

clue.text: Academic knowing about arrest, say

indicators.note: about says the sly letters go around the next piece

parts.note: sly means knowing or cunning

indicators.note: say signals a word spelt as another one sounds

parts.note: to collar is informal for to arrest

explanation.surface: A learned person is shrewd about a police arrest, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' at the end reads like 'for example' but signals a sound-alike; 'about' wraps the knowing word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarly and academic both describe learned, studious work, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Forward's second goal

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A striker scores a second goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a football player but is a verb: to send on, as mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter is to send it on to a new address, so the verbs match.

clue.text: A crowd beginning to knock one activity at Klosters?

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd of people

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mob starts to criticise a pastime at a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Klosters is a Swiss ski resort; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means after skiing: the socialising in bars and chalets at a resort when the slopes close.

clue.text: Hit wood on Birkdale's first

indicators.note: on says the wood comes after the other piece in an across answer
first takes the opening letter of Birkdale

parts.note: ash is a wood from the ash tree

explanation.surface: A golfer strikes with a wooden club at the first hole on Royal Birkdale.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Birkdale is a championship golf course near Southport, England; 'wood' sounds like a golf club but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To bash something is to hit it hard, a synonym.

clue.text: Adult left to get hold of a very strong drink

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: to get hold of says one piece grasps the other inside it

parts.note: quit means left, departed

explanation.surface: A grown-up departs to obtain a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquavit is a Scandinavian caraway-flavoured spirit, so a strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: I can show how it's done — on next EP, possibly

definitions.text: I can show how it's done

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A musician boasts of a demonstration on their next record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ON NEXT EP; an EP is an extended-play record.
explanation.definitionFit: An exponent is someone who expounds or demonstrates a skill, written as the speaker's own claim.

clue.text: Gran cutting cotton cloth

parts.note: nan is an informal word for a grandmother
keen means sharp, as a cutting edge

explanation.surface: Grandma is snipping some cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanking in China.

clue.text: Child supporting celebrity becomes stiff

indicators.note: supporting says the child sits below the celebrity in a down answer

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A kid backing a famous person goes rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff' is the adjective; Chambers gives the word as an adjective too, meaning stiff or formal.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective in Chambers the word means stiff and precise, like starched linen.

clue.text: Packed, needing to stay for a period in America

parts.note: full means packed
to stop is to stay somewhere

explanation.surface: A crowded venue needs somewhere to lodge during a spell in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period' looks like a stretch of time but is the American word for the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call the dot ending a sentence a period; the British name is this phrase.

clue.text: Source of power in English home close to Seascale

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: close to takes the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The power station near Seascale, a village on England's Cumbrian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Seascale is a Cumbrian village beside the Sellafield nuclear site, fitting the power surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine converts fuel into motion and so is a source of mechanical power.

clue.text: Soldier acquired a leg of mutton

parts.note: GI is a US soldier
got means acquired

explanation.surface: A soldier picked up some meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigot is a French culinary term for a leg of lamb or mutton.

clue.text: Certain trees always found on parts of golf courses

parts.note: ever means always
the greens are the areas of short grass around the holes

explanation.surface: Some trees are always growing beside the putting surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees such as pines and holly that keep their leaves all year are a class of trees.

clue.text: Joy requires shelter following onset of gale

indicators.note: following says the shelter comes after the other piece
onset of takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Delight comes from finding cover when a storm begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great delight or merriment, a synonym for joy.

clue.text: Stick around to speak about head of the lodge

indicators.note: about says the spoken word goes around the next piece

parts.note: to say is to speak

indicators.note: head of takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Staying on to chat with the head of a Masonic lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain in a place rather than leave, which is to stick around.

clue.text: Thinks date, abused, was extremely upset

indicators.note: abused says the letters before it are mistreated into a new order

explanation.surface: A person ponders a date that went horribly wrong and is distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges THINKS DATE; the idiom means panicked or got very agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in a state of great agitation or panic means to be very upset.
